newsitem.title: FRANCE: France probes sect over death of two members.
newsitem.headline: France probes sect over death of two members.

text.p: An investigating magistrate has opened a probe into a sect based in southern France after two of its members died apparently for lack of medical care, justice sources said on Thursday.
The sources confirmed a local press report saying the probe into the Horus sect was opened for suspected failure to assist persons in danger after two female members died in 1994 and 1995.
The Horus sect was founded in 1989 in La Coucourde, near Valence.

Police raided the offices of the sect a year ago and checked the health of the members' children. A few months later a judge probed three members of the sect, among them a doctor who had given a falsified vaccination certificate to a sick child.

Earlier this week, police raided the homes in southwestern France of members of a U.S.-based sect called Tabitha's Place after a 19-month-old boy died from malnutrition and an untreated heart ailment. The child's parents were remanded in custody.
French authorities have stepped up surveillance of sects following the grisly deaths of 16 members of the Order of the Solar Temple in southeastern France in December 1995.
